Counting objects that leave and come back

Each detection is placed in 3D using depth and the camera pose, then matched to the objects already found. Scrub through the 60 frames to watch the count build up.

Provisional identities so far

The cup leaves and comes back

The cup is seen in frame 104, is out of view in frame 268, and is back in frame 359. Its returning detection retains the earlier identity. Across the whole clip, the rules create 2 provisional cup identities: a shifted position can start another candidate. Return recovery therefore does not establish a correct physical-object count.

Where it still goes wrong

New objects can appear at any frame. A detection with usable 3D position and no feasible existing match starts a provisional identity, even if other objects of its class already exist. These are candidate identities, not a verified inventory: position noise can split one real object into several candidates.

Grey markers are detections the rules could not assign: 56 of 457.

  • 0 were left unassigned by the historical late-birth restriction. The corrected replay removes that restriction.
  • 37 were close to two known objects at once, too close to call.
  • 10 had no usable depth, so no 3D position.
  • 9 matched an object that another box in the same frame had already claimed.

5 book detections remain unassigned. The next comparison uses the 3D depth samples throughout each box, rather than one median point, to test whether neighbouring objects and repeated sightings can be separated more reliably.

Positions are points on each object's visible surface, read from depth inside its detection box, using the recording's motion-capture camera path rather than our tracker's. They move a little as the camera moves round an object, which is part of the 73 mm spread. There is no surveyed true position for these objects yet.
